why:
LANDED (phase-444) — ADOPTED, and the one row in this family that needed CODE rather than a corrected verdict. Every other graph gap was a receiver difference recorded as an absence; this pair was genuinely missing.

WHAT WE SHIP: `rclc_executor_wait_for_publishers` (`nros_generated.h`), a thin wrapper (RFC-0019/0020) over `Executor::wait_for_publishers` (`nros-node/src/executor/spin.rs`), which polls the shipped `count_publishers` between cooperative `spin_once` calls.

WHY BLOCKING IS ALLOWED HERE. This is the only blocking member of the graph family, and it does NOT weaken the family's never-blocks contract — it COMPOSES it. The query underneath still reports only what has been DISCOVERED and still never blocks; what waits is the loop, by polling that query. RFC-0021 is the rule that governs it and it does not forbid blocking: it requires a blocking helper to take an executor and DRIVE it, which is what makes the timeout reliable on a single-threaded transport and what makes the reentrancy visible at the call site. `rclc_client_wait_for_service` is the same construction one entity kind over, and it ships. `declined` was considered and rejected for exactly that reason: declining this while shipping `wait_for_service` would be two verdicts for one fact, which is the incoherence the other sixteen rows in this shard were.

ONE DELIBERATE DIFFERENCE FROM `wait_for_service`: a backend that cannot read the graph returns `UNSUPPORTED` IMMEDIATELY instead of waiting out the budget. `wait_for_service` waits and reports a timeout (issue 1087) because a service that is not yet answerable is a TRANSIENT. A backend with no graph (XRCE) is PERMANENT, so spending the budget to report a timeout would say "none appeared" about a backend that cannot see endpoints at all — collapsing "cannot tell you" into "not there", which is the distinction RFC-0036 exists to keep and which every other method in this family promises. Mutation-tested: copying `wait_for_service`'s policy here turns the test red with `Ok(false)`.

`count == 0` is satisfied without asking the backend at all — "at least zero" is true of every graph and needs no discovery, so it holds even where the graph cannot be read.

IT STAYS A DIVERGENCE ON THE RECEIVER, for the reason the whole family does: rcl hangs this off a NODE (`rcl_wait_for_publishers(node, allocator, ...)`) because each node owns a participant; we open ONE session per image and the Executor owns it. Our C convention is `nros_<receiver>_<verb>`, so the receiver is in the name. Upstream also takes an allocator and writes through a `bool *success`; ours returns `RCL_RET_OK` / `RCL_RET_TIMEOUT` / `RCL_RET_UNSUPPORTED` / `RCLC_RET_REENTRANT` and allocates nothing.

Blocks until at least `count` publishers are on a topic, or the timeout expires. The startup-ordering primitive a volatile-durability talker needs before its first `publish`.
